correctness.rationale: If coprime inputs have equal abundancy, the denominator of the common reduced fraction divides both inputs, so the common value is an integer. Exact comparison of the five exponent partitions of total multiplicity four gives a global maximum below 3, while the same five partitions on odd primes give a maximum below 2. Lower multiplicities embed into the four-factor layer by multiplying by fresh primes, which strictly increases abundancy. Thus distinct coprime low-multiplicity inputs would have common abundancy 2 and both be even, contradicting coprimality. All displayed maxima were recomputed exactly with rational arithmetic.

value.rationale: The claim closes a natural first nonsquarefree complexity range of an explicit open distinctness problem. Total prime-factor multiplicity is intrinsic to the divisor-sum product, and \(\Omega=4\) is the last layer on which the elementary odd-deficiency barrier used here is uniformly available; odd abundant numbers already occur at multiplicity five. The theorem therefore identifies a mathematically motivated boundary rather than an arbitrary finite cutoff, and it complements the known squarefree slice by admitting every repeated-prime exponent pattern through that boundary.
